U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.locator_convention: Original separately served facsimiles; a/b denote left/right printed columns. No local PDF pagination.
U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.verification: Both original pages directly viewed; online entry used as a finding aid. Quantities/spelling in examples are BT’s own and are not silently converted to Cook.
U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.claim: The entry distinguishes uninflected participles from inflected and mixed usage with habban. The object may be described by an accusative participle; the finite auxiliary still agrees with its subject. Bare and agreeing realizations are evidenced alternatives, not an exceptionless mapping from English perfect grammar.

exact_examples.analysis: Plural finite subject Hie contrasts with singular accusative hine/ofslægenne. This is evidence for object-linked participial inflection, not participle agreement with the finite subject.

exact_examples.text: Ðú hafast helle bereáfod and ðæs deáþes aldor gebundenne
exact_examples.analysis: The coordinated example combines a bare participle with an inflected accusative-masculine participle referring to the object aldor.

U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.evidence_limits: Use the selected bare bases for Unit12 production. Recognize or accept appropriately agreeing alternatives only where their actual inflection and lexical use are supported. These evidence examples are not added learner tasks, vocabulary assignments or assigned source reading. No general causative or every historical perfect use is introduced.

U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-SUPPLEMENT.original_identifier: habban,B auxiliary subsection(1)(a),(1)(b),(2), printed493a; entry begins491b and continues492
U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-SUPPLEMENT.locator_convention: Original separately served supplement facsimiles; a/b denote columns. No local PDF pagination.
U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-SUPPLEMENT.verification: All three original pages directly viewed. The main entry and the supplement have separate printed pagination.
U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-SUPPLEMENT.claim: The auxiliary subsection directly distinguishes present habban with inflected or uninflected participles and past habban in a pluperfect construction. A preceding object-complement subsection also gives causative/resultative uses; these are not all the same syntactic or semantic construction.
U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-SUPPLEMENT.evidence_limits: Corroborates optional participial inflection and contextual tense interpretation. Unit12 does not teach arbitrary causative habban, all intransitive have-perfects, or the other lexical habban senses catalogued here.

decision: Selected uninflected bases remain the productive model; finite auxiliary agreement is separate from any object-linked participial agreement. Evidenced alternatives should not be rejected merely for differing from that model. Full new participial adjective declensions are not silently assigned.
independence: Coordinator performed this source check after the grammar analyst identified the evidence gap, before final audit reconciliation or learner/key drafting.
